records.company: Telent Technology Services Ltd (part of M Group)
records.title: Graduate Network Engineer
records.location: Farnborough, UK (Telecom division; two-year programme with six-month rotations)
records.clearance_check: Pass — no clearance stated. Standard 2:2 STEM degree requirement, no sponsorship restriction stated in the posting.
records.work_authorisation_risk: Not assessed — owner instruction 2026-10-03: do not discuss visa status for any application.
records.key_gap: The posting asks for a minimum 2:2 Honours Degree in a relevant STEM subject achieved within the last two years. The owner holds an MSc Information Security (Merit, Sep 2025) and a BCA in computing (CGPA 9.17, Sep 2024) — both within the window and both STEM. Directly evidenced: troubleshooting, server health monitoring, access control administration, security fundamentals, documentation, team coordination. Not evidenced and not claimed: enterprise routing/switching configuration (Cisco/Juniper), CCNA or equivalent networking certification, firewall administration, cloud platform deployment (AWS/Azure networking specifically), network automation tooling (Ansible/Terraform), IET accreditation progress.
records.recommendation: Applied per owner standing instruction. Fit is moderate and honest: this is an operational network and infrastructure role, and the owner's nearest genuine evidence is IT support with network-adjacent duties (network and website-access controls, server health monitoring, access requests, endpoint troubleshooting) plus security fundamentals from the MSc and certifications. The networking-specific configuration gap is real and is not overstated in the documents; the CV and cover letter lead on troubleshooting method, security-aware reasoning and documented operational support, which is what a graduate network engineer actually does in year one.
